## Summary

I created a SPARQL query retrieving all professors meeting the three criteria, using **2025-08-16** as the reference date.

**My reading of each requirement:**
1. **Full professors** — In the data, roles are either `"Professor of X"` (full) or `"Assistant Professor of X"`. Since no "Associate" ranks exist, I filter to roles containing "professor" but excluding "assistant professor".
2. **EU-located department** — At least one department the professor works in belongs to a university whose `locatedInCountry` is one of the 27 EU member states as of 2025-08-16 (list encoded as ISO alpha-2 codes; excludes CH, US, GB).
3. **>10 currently-enrolled students** — At least one department they work in has more than 10 distinct *currently-enrolled* students across any course `isTaughtIn` that department. "Currently enrolled" = enrollment date ≤ reference date and not graduated by the reference date (no graduation date, or graduation date > 2025-08-16).

I kept the **qualification conditions separate from the output**: `?countries` lists *all* countries where the professor works (via `worksIn`), not just the EU or qualifying ones — hence Orfeas Menis shows both `GR` and `US`.

| professorName | countries |
|---|---|

| Pepe Attanasio | PT, GR |

A diagnostic confirmed the qualifying departments: ComputerScience_NTUA (12) and HistoryAndPhilosophy_NKUA (12) exceed 10; Engineering_Berkeley (11) is US (fails criterion 2 and has no full professor); Mathematics_Sorbonne (6, Marie Dubois) and Biology_MIT (7, John Smith) correctly fail. Assistant professors (Voulodimos, Mueller) are correctly excluded by criterion 1.
